title: Send unroutable parcels to the hold shelf

blocks.text: The depot's sorter sends each parcel to a bin by the first two characters of its postcode. Since the depot started accepting parcels before the recipient's details are complete, the sorter stops dead now and then with a `NullPointerException`, and every parcel behind the one it choked on waits. Those parcels should go to the `HOLD` shelf instead, and the rest should keep moving.

`Sorting` already has the three steps from a parcel to its postcode, and `binFor(...)` turns a postcode into a bin. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/Sorting.java`: `postcodeOf(...)` returns the parcel's postcode, or nothing when the depot can't route the parcel yet, whichever of its parts is missing. About four lines.

cases.says: a parcel with a recipient, an address and a postcode gets that postcode and its bin
a recipient with no address, a null in the middle of the chain, gives no postcode instead of an exception
a parcel with no recipient, a null after the first step, gives no postcode instead of an exception
an address with no postcode gives no postcode

origin.section: A null Halfway Through an andThen Chain Fails in the Next Step; Optional.map Stops There

concepts: andThen passes a null result on to the next step, which throws; Optional.map stops at the first null, so the steps after it don't run.
